methodology:
Astarta Holding refined from 1-row to 5-row breakdown reflecting both geographic and business-segment splits. Per Astarta's own FY24 disclosures:
- Poltava Oblast: 129,000 ha (60%) — largest land bank; supports 3 sugar plants (Yareskivsky, Globinsky, Novoorzhytskyi) + soybean processing + biogas + oil extraction at Hlobine
- Khmelnytsky Oblast: 42,000 ha (20%) — Western Ukraine, supports Volochysk sugar plant
- Vinnytsia Oblast: 16,000 ha (7%) + other regions: ~33K ha (13%)

Plus 22,000-head dairy operation with supporting fodder cropland.

5-row breakdown:
- Poltava cropland (318.7K ac / 129K ha): largest single cluster, central Ukraine
- Khmelnytsky cropland (103.8K ac / 42K ha): Western Ukraine slight EU-proximity premium
- Vinnytsia + other (39.5K ac / 16K ha)
- Downstream processing: 5 sugar plants + soybean + biogas + oil extraction (placeholder, per-acre meaningless)
- Dairy + fodder support (80K ac including dairy facilities + supporting cropland)

Per-acre marks reflect post-2022 wartime discount. Pre-war Ukrainian cropland traded at $2,000-3,000/acre USD; current 2024 transactions in central regions at $400-800/acre with western Ukraine slightly higher. Astarta's land bank is concentrated in safer central-Ukraine regions.

Wartime context: FY25 revenue fell 23% to €472M as sugar volumes declined; net profit fell 4.2x. Land FMV stable but reflects deep wartime discount. Peace-scenario revaluation back to pre-war levels would imply 3-5x higher per-acre values.
